quotes.text: Governance in Microsoft Fabric isn't difficult because the features are missing. It's difficult because the systems refuse to speak the same language.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Pinpoints the real cause of Fabric governance pain.

quotes.text: The platforms are brilliant at storing facts, but hopeless at reasoning about them. They can tell you what exists, but not how those things relate in context.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why cross-service compliance needs reasoning, not just data.

quotes.text: Most users mistake reasoning for verbosity. They assume a longer explanation means the models showing off. No, the verbosity is evidence of deliberation.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes long AI answers as an audit trail.

quotes.text: Governance becomes ambient. Audits no longer interrupt projects. They accompany them like background compilation. Designers perceive security not as bureaucracy, but as hygiene, always present, seldom obstructive.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Describes the cultural shift toward continuous compliance.

takeaways: Fabric, Purview and Power BI each hold part of the governance picture, which makes manual cross-checks slow and error-prone.
GPT-5 reasoning in Copilot correlates lineage, classifications and row-level security across services in a single query and documents its reasoning steps.
In Copilot Studio, enable the GPT-5 model, connect Fabric, Power BI and Purview via connectors, build reusable audit prompts, test with staged anomalies and keep validating results.
hook: Governance teams still spend weeks reconciling Purview classifications, Power BI security and Fabric lineage in spreadsheets. This episode explains to data governance and compliance leads how GPT-5 reasoning in Copilot and Copilot Studio can automate those cross-service audits while keeping a verifiable audit trail.
